proof_summary: Factoring each factorial into its powers of \(p\) and its \(p\)-free part reduces the even-index case to a lifted Wilson congruence modulo \(q^3\), \(q=p^{t+1}\); this congruence follows by pairing reduced residues under \(u\mapsto q-u\) and using \(\sum u^{-2}=0\pmod q\) to eliminate the quadratic error. For odd indices, splitting the reduced residues into half-ranges and applying doubling yields a generalized Morley relation between the central shifted block and the ordinary reduced-residue block, which cancels the extra powers of \(2\) and gives the same one-step congruence; taking \(t=r-1\) completes the argument.
